Below is what can be established from the visible evidence.

1) Proposal: Network controls & fixed egress IP for sandboxes
- Author: Michael Xu
- Timestamp: Jul 6th at 2:46 PM
- Concise proposal (from initial message):
  "hey everyone - feature request (or a conversation if this is already supported) - ive been trialing daytona, and it's been great so far and has everything we need.. with the exception of a few things.
   is there any way to introspect or inject at the network for a sandbox? we are using daytona to host customer apps - but because these apps are most likely vibe coded, having some controls outside of the sandbox (don't allow network egress except for these URLs), or the ability to inject authorization headers, outside the sandbox, is very important.
   is there a way to have a fixed egress IP? we connect to customer resources and having a static IP would be really nice so I dont have to workaround this."
  Summary: Request for (a) network-level controls for sandboxes (egress restrictions to specified URLs, ability to inject auth headers outside the sandbox) and (b) a fixed/static egress IP for connecting to customer resources.
- Visible reaction count: 2 reactions (1 eyes emoji, 1 white check mark emoji), as indicated by two separate buttons:
  - "1 reaction, react with eyes emoji"
  - "1 reaction, react with white check mark emoji"
- Visible reply count: 7 replies (explicitly shown as "7 replies").
- Explicitly stated benefits/concerns from its thread:
  • Concern/need: Because customer apps are “most likely vibe coded,” there is a need for controls *outside* the sandbox:
    - Control network egress (e.g., "don't allow network egress except for these URLs").
    - Inject authorization headers outside the sandbox.
    - Have a fixed egress IP so customer firewalls can allowlist a known static IP and avoid workarounds.
  • From replies by Dalin Stone (summary from visible text):
    - For static egress IPs, the recommended approach is to use a VPN connection with Tailscale and route sandbox traffic through an exit node with a known static IP. This gives full control over what to allowlist and ensures all sandbox traffic appears from a single IP from the firewall’s perspective.
    - This works out of the box in Daytona because Tailscale falls back to TCP when UDP isn’t available.
    - A guide for this is available at: daytona.io/docs/en/vpn-connections#…
    - Earlier replies indicate “Yep we have this” (for injecting or using secrets) and reference daytona.io/docs/en/secrets, suggesting that existing “secrets” functionality might address part of the request.
    - Later in the thread:
      • Michael Xu notes that he initially misunderstood the “secrets” feature, thinking it was only for mounting secrets in a volume, and expresses that the existing capability is “great.”
      • Michael asks another question about injecting credentials via this feature to git or Claude; Dalin replies "This works for anything, yep," indicating broad applicability of the secrets-based credential injection.
  • Implicit benefit: Increased control and safety for customer apps (fine‑grained egress control, static egress IP) and easier integration with customer firewalls and protected resources.

2) Post: Firecracker guest image benchmarking (not a direct feature request)
- Author: Gautam Talks
- Timestamp: Aug 10th at 4:51:36 PM (shown as "Aug 10th at 4:51:36 PM").
- Concise content summary:
  "Not a feature request, but hopefully useful. I spent a few weeks benchmarking Firecracker guest images and published the harnesses: github.com/GautamTalksDev/mayfly-guest
   Main finding: most published kernel-stripping advice for Firecracker is stale. Turning ACPI off costs 278ms rather than saving time, because modern Firecracker passes device info through ACPI tables and MPTable booting is now deprecated. Disabling PCI breaks root disk discovery entirely, since CONFIG_PCI is required for guest …"
  Summary: Sharing benchmarking results and harnesses for Firecracker guest images. Key finding is that much existing kernel‑stripping guidance is outdated; disabling ACPI and PCI harms boot performance and functionality.
- Visible reaction count: 1 reaction (white check mark), as indicated by:

- Visible reply count: Not visible in the current snapshot; there is no explicit "X replies" element shown for this message, and no thread panel is open for it.
- Explicitly stated benefit/concern from its thread: None visible; only the main post is captured, with no visible replies in the current view.
  • Benefit (from message text itself): Provides updated empirical guidance on Firecracker guest configuration that avoids performance regressions (ACPI off adds ~278ms) and boot breakage (disabling PCI breaks root disk discovery).

3) Post: Announcement of Spot GPU sandboxes
- Author: Daytona (workspace app/user labeled "Daytona").
- Timestamp: Aug 20th at 8:38:49 AM.
- Concise proposal/announcement (core text):
  "Daytona: Spot GPU sandboxes are now live for everyone! Run GPU workloads on preemptible capacity at a fraction of on-demand pricing:
   • No quotas: spot GPUs don't count against your GPU quota. Available capacity is the only limit.
   • Deeply discounted: significantly cheaper than on-demand GPUs, see the pricing page: https://www.daytona.io/pricing
   • All GPU types: H100, H200, RTX Pro 6000, RTX 4090, RTX 5090, with ordered fallback between types.

   Getting started: choose a GPU, set resources, and use any Docker image:
   sandbox = daytona.create(
       CreateSandboxFromImageParams(
           image="nvidia/cuda:12.4.1-base-ubuntu22.04",
           auto_delete_interval=0,
           spot=True,
           resources=Resources(gpu=1, gpu_type=GpuType.H100),
       )
   )

   Heads up: spot sandboxes are preemptible. They can be reclaimed at any time when on-demand capacity is needed, so design workloads to tolerate interruption. Preempted sandboxes get a spotEvictedAt timestamp and stay retrievable for 24 hours.

   Try it: https://app.daytona.io/
   Docs: https://www.daytona.io/docs/sandboxes#spot-gpu-sandboxes
